source.title: Product-Stability: Provable Convergence for Gradient Descent on the Edge of Stability

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Analyzes gradient-descent convergence at the edge of stability using a factored loss and reports CIFAR-10 training dynamics, bearing conceptually on V5.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical convergence for factored objectives and CIFAR-10 training loss and sharpness behavior. Cited results from other papers are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional convergence beyond the stability threshold for factored objectives and reports its own neural-network loss and sharpness trajectories at the edge of stability, bearing on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate: product-stable minima give local, conditional GD convergence for l(xy), and stronger initialization conditions yield a precise final-sharpness prediction. The CIFAR-10 experiment shows decreasing long-term loss, oscillatory sharpness and positive product-stability; it does not establish a convergence theorem for deep networks. The authors explicitly leave global dynamics and progressive sharpening unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Studies a factored scalar loss theoretically and a two-class CIFAR-10 tanh network; it does not reproduce the cited squared-loss wide-network or full-batch protocols.
record.method_sensitivity: The CIFAR-10 experiments use η = 0.05 and η = 0.02, with corresponding stated EoS thresholds of 40 and 100. The theorem requires an initialization gap above the threshold; Figure 3 is described as showing nonconvergence to its predicted final sharpness when started very close to the threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: The CIFAR-10 experiments have positive multivariate product-stability during EoS training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Positive multivariate product-stability accompanies stable EoS training in the tested tanh network; this diagnostic alone does not establish loss recovery or convergence.

record.problems: The real-world experiment is a fully connected network on a two-class, 5,000-example CIFAR-10 subset. The text gives qualitative descriptions of the plotted loss and sharpness but no numerical result values or uncertainty estimates. The theoretical analysis is local, and the authors say it does not explain progressive sharpening.

untested.parts: Training classification error in large convolutional networks, corrupted or random labels, and effects of size, early stopping or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies and extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, special initializations or Fixup.
Initialization comparisons, training speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.

The initial loss-rise catapult in wide squared-loss networks; divergence at larger learning rates or from below the initial threshold. The local theory does not explain progressive sharpening into the EoS regime. Section 7 does not specify the training loss function or explicitly document batch size.
Batch-normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and normalization-free Fixup training.

missing.what: Theorem 5.2 predicts final sharpness 2/η − [3(l''(z*))^4/α_l(z*)]η + O(η^(5/3)), with an additional positive initialization gap δ.
Own toy experiments with factored BCE with soft target 2/3 and multilayer squared loss show oscillatory loss, movement toward lower sharpness and convergence just below the stability threshold.

Initialization very close to the threshold does not produce the final sharpness predicted by Theorem 5.2, demonstrating the need for its initialization-gap condition. This is not reported as failure to converge.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its theoretical restrictions and untested claim components do not independently warrant limits_scope. The supplied text contains qualitative figure descriptions but no readable plot values beyond the stated thresholds.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size comparisons and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious minima frequency and student width.
Plain versus residual shortcut networks, depth comparisons and normalization.
Comparisons of initialization methods and trainable depth.
Does not test squared-loss wide networks or full-batch sharpness dynamics over longer timescales as in the version's cited studies; its real-world model uses a two-class CIFAR-10 subset.
Batch-normalization speed or learning-rate tolerance comparisons, and Fixup.

rows.subject: L(x, y) = l(xy)
rows.size_stated: two parameters, interpreted as a two-layer, single-neuron linear model
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 4.3 gives gradient-descent convergence near a product-stable minimum when the initial sharpness multiplier is slightly above the edge-of-stability threshold.

conditions.value: l has a local minimum z* with l''(z*) > 0 and αl(z*) > 0

rows.note: The result is conditional and theoretical; it does not establish convergence for arbitrary deep networks.
rows.check: Retain as a conditional theoretical result. The initialization condition concerns l''(z*)s0, which equals sharpness at a stationary point; it is not an exact measurement of initial sharpness away from that point. Theorem 4.3 permits initialization at the threshold and requires no positive gap δ; that additional condition belongs to Theorem 5.2.

rows.subject: fully connected tanh network
rows.operation_detail: Gradient-descent training on a two-class subset of CIFAR-10; the paper reports training loss behavior.
rows.value: consistently decreases over long timescales and oscillates while in the EoS regime
rows.note: The text describes both learning-rate scenarios together; it does not give a separate numeric loss for this rate.
rows.check: The qualitative value is supported by the captions and Section 7, so evidence is not figure-only. No numerical final loss or initial catapult rise is reported.

rows.subject: fully connected tanh network
rows.measure: Sharpness relative to the edge-of-stability threshold
rows.value: training enters the EoS regime with sharpness greater than the EoS threshold; sharpness oscillates around the threshold
rows.note: The paper states the threshold values for both rates but does not assign a separate sharpness value to this rate.
rows.check: Correct the baseline from η/2 to 2/η = 40. Section 7 and the Figure 5 caption explicitly report the qualitative behavior.
